name: Chukwuemeka Oko
missingPieces: D1 omits the stored XSS finding entirely and has no XXE entry in the catalogue; D2 mislabels the 02:18:47 stored-XSS beacon as XXE and drops the open-redirect hop (02:21:13); CVSS vectors are mostly unjustified and SQLi is scored A:H instead of A:N; impact naira is churn-cost based, not derived from the exfil-sample balances; D4 cites NDPA Section 37 rather than the breach-notification sections 40/41.
feedback: D1 is the strongest part of your catalogue and your method section is exactly what we want, you read all five files, mapped each request to a source line, and treated the developer comments as clues rather than truth. Findings 1 to 5 (SQL injection CWE-89 lines 64-67, unsalted MD5 CWE-916 line 66, JWT alg:none CWE-347 lines 48-49, hard-coded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 CWE-321 line 30, and no token expiry CWE-613) are all proven with a quoted line and a correct class, and you correctly resisted calling alg:none the decoy, it is a real bug honoured by the shared service. Your decoy adjudication on the b64url helpers is excellent, you proved at the mechanism level that they are RFC 4648 formatting, not crypto, and named the truly dangerous constructs. Where D1 loses points is two substantial findings missing, there is no stored XSS finding at all (the comment beacon firing a cookie to 185.220.101.9:8443) and no XXE entry in the catalogue, so the 6-and-7 row scores nothing. D2 is the weakest deliverable. You reconciled SQLi at 02:15:31, the 312-row pull at 02:16:04, and the path-traversal read at 02:24:02 to their capture lines, but you mislabeled the 02:18:47 line as XXE when that line is the stored-XSS script beacon, the XXE runs in parallel through import.php, and you dropped the open-redirect hop at 02:21:13 entirely, so your chain is about half reconciled. Your CVSS vectors are complete strings, but most carry no justifying sentence and several are wrong, the SQLi auth bypass does not touch availability so it is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1, not A:H at 9.8, and your SameSite vector at C:H/I:H/A:H 8.8 is not defensible. Your impact correctly anchors on 312 customers and states assumptions, which we reward, but the naira figure of 15.6M is a churn-and-notification estimate rather than a sum of the account balances in the exfil sample (balances up to roughly 950k summing into tens of millions), and you missed the BoltCash launch in about six weeks as the multiplier. D3 reads well, the executive summary is genuinely jargon-free and your threat model and earliest-break fix (WAF rule plus secret rotation at hop 4) are clear, and crucially your remediation order is built on risk reduction per hour of effort, a 15-minute WAF rule first and a 30-minute secret rotation second, which is the effort-to-risk framing we ask for rather than blind CVSS ordering. Your two detection stopgaps each give an exact field and a false-positive estimate, which earns most of that row. D4 is your best deliverable, you answer all four prompts in your own voice with a clear decision to refuse comment and route to Comms, you cite ISC2 Canon I and II by number load-bearing, and you anchor to your own findings (the line 29 rotate-before-prod note, the 312 records, the Ngozi objection). The one slip in D4 is the NDPA section, you cited Section 37 (security measures) when the breach-notification duty you describe is Section 40 (notify the NDPC within 72 hours) and Section 41 (notify data subjects on high risk), so tie the 72-hour clock to Section 40 next time. There is no fabrication here, your evidence lines trace to the pack and your impact is assumption-based rather than invented, so no penalty applies. The single most important fix is to catalogue every distinct finding and reconcile each chain hop to its true capture line, you lost the most ground by missing stored XSS and by mislabeling the 02:18:47 beacon as XXE while dropping the open-redirect hop.
